questions.stem: A candle flame uses oxygen, gives off carbon dioxide and gets bigger when fed with wax. The flame is still regarded as non-living mainly because it cannot
questions.explanation: Fire shows some features of life but cannot produce offspring like itself, so it is non-living.

questions.stem: Which characteristic of living things is shown when a bean seedling kept in a dark cupboard bends towards a small hole that admits light?
questions.explanation: Responding to a stimulus such as light is irritability (sensitivity).

questions.stem: Organisms whose cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus are placed in the kingdom
questions.explanation: Monera (bacteria and blue-green bacteria) are prokaryotes without a true nucleus.

questions.stem: A green, single-celled organism moves with a flagellum, has an eyespot and can feed holozoically in the dark. It is best placed in the kingdom
questions.explanation: Euglena-like organisms are eukaryotic unicells and are grouped in Protoctista.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups contains ONLY members of the kingdom Fungi?
questions.explanation: Yeast, Mucor and mushroom are all fungi; Spirogyra, moss, Amoeba and fern are not.

questions.stem: Which of the following is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Only plant cells have a cellulose cell wall; the others occur in both.

questions.stem: Plants generally show growth at the tips of roots and shoots, while most animals
options: grow only at the head region
grow in all parts of the body
questions.explanation: Plant growth is localised at meristems, while animal growth is diffuse throughout the body.

questions.stem: The correct sequence of increasing complexity of organisation is
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form systems.

questions.stem: A colony of Volvox is regarded as an example of organisation at the level of
questions.explanation: Volvox is a colony of similar cells loosely co-operating, i.e. a cell aggregate.

questions.stem: The heart of a mammal is regarded as an organ because it
options: is found in the chest cavity
is made of only one kind of cell
pumps blood to the lungs only
is made of different tissues working together
beats continuously throughout the life of the animal
questions.explanation: An organ is a structure made of several tissues performing a common function.

questions.topic: Complexity of organization in higher organisms
questions.stem: An advantage of the division of labour in a multicellular organism is that
options: every cell can live independently of others
cells do not need oxygen any longer
each cell type performs its task more efficiently
the organism no longer needs a nervous or transport system
every cell carries out all life processes
questions.explanation: Specialisation allows cells to become efficient at particular functions.

questions.topic: Forms in which Living Cells Exist
questions.stem: Which of the following exists as a free-living single cell?
questions.explanation: Paramecium is unicellular; Volvox is colonial, Spirogyra filamentous and Hydra multicellular.

questions.topic: Forms in which Living Cells Exist
questions.stem: Which pair of organisms shows the colonial form of cell existence?
questions.explanation: Volvox and Pandorina are colonial green algae.

questions.stem: The organelle in which aerobic respiration releases most of the energy of a cell is the
questions.explanation: The Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation take place in the mitochondria.

questions.stem: Which cell structure controls the substances that enter and leave the cell?
questions.explanation: The partially permeable cell membrane regulates exchange of materials.

questions.stem: A cell from the pancreas that secretes large amounts of enzymes would be expected to have an especially well-developed
options: contractile vacuoles together with numerous cilia and flagella
cellulose wall and large central vacuole
rough endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus
questions.explanation: Secretory cells make protein on rough ER and package it in the Golgi apparatus.

questions.stem: When red blood cells are placed in distilled water, they swell and burst. This bursting is called
questions.explanation: Water enters by osmosis and the cell bursts, a process called haemolysis.

questions.stem: A strip of pawpaw tissue placed in a strong salt solution became soft and shorter. This is because its cells
options: took in air through the cut ends
questions.explanation: The salt solution is hypertonic, so water leaves the cells and they become flaccid.

questions.stem: Root hair cells take up nitrate ions from soil where the nitrate concentration is lower than in the cell sap. This uptake requires
options: the absence of oxygen in the soil
water moving out of the cells
questions.explanation: Movement against a concentration gradient is active transport, which uses ATP from respiration.

questions.stem: A plant cell that has lost so much water that the cytoplasm pulls away from the cell wall is said to be
questions.explanation: Shrinkage of the protoplast away from the wall is plasmolysis.

questions.stem: Euglena can make its food in light but feeds on organic matter in darkness. This mode of feeding is described as
questions.explanation: Combining autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition is mixotrophic nutrition.

questions.stem: The end products of aerobic respiration of glucose are
questions.explanation: Glucose is completely oxidised to carbon dioxide and water, releasing energy.

questions.stem: During vigorous exercise, the muscles of an athlete accumulate
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration in muscles produces lactic acid, causing an oxygen debt.

questions.stem: Taking the textbook values of 38 ATP per glucose molecule for aerobic respiration and 2 ATP for anaerobic respiration in yeast, how many times as much ATP does aerobic respiration yield?
questions.explanation: 38 / 2 = 19 times as much ATP.

questions.stem: In Amoeba, excess water is removed from the cell by the
questions.explanation: The contractile vacuole collects and expels excess water (osmoregulation).

questions.stem: Most nitrogenous waste in Amoeba is lost as ammonia by
options: storage in the contractile vacuole until the cell divides into two
questions.explanation: Ammonia is very soluble and diffuses out over the large surface of the cell.

questions.stem: An increase in dry mass of an organism that is permanent is known as
questions.explanation: Growth is a permanent increase in size and dry mass.

questions.stem: In plants, growth in length takes place mainly in the
questions.explanation: Cells of apical meristems at root and shoot tips divide to increase length.

questions.stem: Cells at a root tip that have stopped dividing elongate, develop thick lignified walls and lose their end walls to become xylem vessels. This change in form and function is
questions.explanation: Development involves cell differentiation into specialised cell types.

questions.stem: Paramecium moves by beating its
questions.explanation: Paramecium is covered with cilia that beat in co-ordinated waves.

questions.stem: Cytoplasmic streaming that pushes out pseudopodia is the means of movement in
questions.explanation: Amoeba moves by amoeboid movement, the flow of cytoplasm into pseudopodia.

questions.stem: Yeast commonly reproduces asexually by
questions.explanation: Yeast cells produce small outgrowths (buds) that separate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of asexual reproduction?
options: Offspring are produced quickly from one parent
It increases the ability of offspring to resist new diseases
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction is rapid and needs only one parent.

questions.stem: Conjugation in Spirogyra involves
options: release of spores from a sporangium
breaking of a filament into short fragments that each grow into new filaments
fusion of contents of two cells from different filaments
splitting of one cell into two equal halves
growth of a bud from the side of a cell
questions.explanation: In conjugation, contents of one cell pass through a tube to fuse with another, forming a zygospore.

questions.topic: Skeleton and supporting systems in animals
questions.stem: The skeleton of an insect is made mainly of
questions.explanation: Insects have a chitinous exoskeleton.

questions.topic: Skeleton and supporting systems in animals
questions.stem: Which type of joint is found between the humerus and the ulna?
questions.explanation: The elbow is a hinge joint, allowing movement in one plane.

questions.topic: Skeleton and supporting systems in animals
questions.stem: The atlas vertebra differs from the axis vertebra in that the atlas
options: lacks a centrum and has large facets for the skull
questions.explanation: The atlas has no centrum and broad articulating facets for the occipital condyles; the axis bears the odontoid process.

questions.topic: Skeleton and supporting systems in animals
questions.stem: When the arm is bent at the elbow, the
options: ligaments contract to pull the radius
triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes
biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes
questions.explanation: Biceps and triceps are antagonistic; the biceps contracts to flex the arm.

questions.stem: The tissue that gives mechanical support to young herbaceous stems by having cells thickened at the corners is
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells have extra cellulose at their corners.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a supporting tissue made of dead cells with walls thickened with lignin?
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma fibres are dead, lignified cells.

questions.stem: Herbaceous plants such as Amaranthus are kept upright mainly by
questions.explanation: Turgor pressure in parenchyma cells supports non-woody plants.

questions.stem: Blood is carried from the heart to the lungs by the
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

questions.stem: Which blood component helps in the clotting of blood?
options: Plasma proteins of the albumin type
questions.explanation: Platelets release substances that start the clotting process.

questions.stem: A man has a resting heart rate of 72 beats per minute and a stroke volume of 70 cm3. What volume of blood does his heart pump in one minute?
questions.explanation: Cardiac output = 72 x 70 = 5040 cm3 per minute.

questions.stem: Valves are present in veins but absent in arteries mainly because blood in veins
options: flows away from the heart towards the capillaries at all times
flows at low pressure and could flow backwards
questions.explanation: Venous blood is at low pressure; valves prevent backflow.

questions.topic: Uptake and movement of water and mineral salts in plants
questions.stem: Water enters the root hair cells from the soil mainly by
questions.explanation: Soil water is more dilute than root hair cell sap, so water enters by osmosis.

questions.topic: Uptake and movement of water and mineral salts in plants
questions.stem: Water passes from the root cortex into the xylem after crossing the
questions.explanation: All water must pass through the endodermis to enter the stele.

questions.stem: Manufactured food is transported in flowering plants through the
questions.explanation: Translocation of sugars occurs in phloem sieve tubes.

questions.stem: When a ring of bark is removed from a woody stem, a swelling forms above the ring after some weeks. This shows that
options: the stem is losing water through the cut
water moving up the xylem is blocked
the cambium above the ring has stopped dividing and the tissue has died
food moving down in the phloem is blocked at the ring
the roots are absorbing more water
questions.explanation: Ringing removes phloem; sugars accumulate above the cut, causing swelling.

questions.stem: Loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant is called
questions.explanation: Transpiration is evaporative water loss, mainly through stomata.

questions.stem: Which condition will INCREASE the rate of transpiration in a plant?
questions.explanation: Wind, low humidity, high temperature and light all increase transpiration.

questions.stem: A leafy shoot in a potometer took up 0.6 cm3 of water in 15 minutes. The rate of water uptake per hour is
questions.explanation: 0.6 / 15 x 60 = 2.4 cm3 per hour.

questions.topic: Movement of water to the apex of trees and herbs
questions.stem: The continuity of the water column in xylem vessels depends mainly on the
options: storage of starch in the pith
activity of guard cells at night
questions.explanation: Cohesion of water molecules (and adhesion to vessel walls) keeps the column unbroken.

questions.stem: The respiratory surface of a bony fish is the
questions.explanation: Fish exchange gases across gill filaments.

questions.stem: Air enters the lungs of a mammal when the
questions.explanation: Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostals increases thoracic volume, lowering pressure.

questions.stem: Which feature of the alveolus does NOT directly increase the rate of gaseous exchange?
options: Presence of ciliated cells lining its wall
questions.explanation: Alveoli are not ciliated; cilia line the trachea and bronchi.

questions.stem: Coiled tubes called nephridia, found in pairs in almost every body segment, carry out excretion in the
questions.explanation: Earthworms excrete through paired segmental nephridia.

questions.stem: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of
questions.explanation: Insects excrete uric acid through Malpighian tubules.

questions.stem: Flowering plants get rid of some of their waste substances by
options: filtering them through nephridia in the stem
passing them out through Malpighian tubules attached to the base of the stem
releasing them as urea through the root hairs
pumping them out with contractile vacuoles
depositing them in leaves and bark that are later shed
questions.explanation: Plants store wastes such as tannins and crystals in leaves and bark which fall off.

questions.stem: The functional unit of the mammalian kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons.

questions.stem: After drinking very little water on a hot day, a student passes a small volume of concentrated urine. This is mainly because more
options: antidiuretic hormone makes the collecting ducts reabsorb water
insulin makes the glomerulus filter less blood and less salt into the nephron
urea is converted back to amino acids
glucose is reabsorbed in the loop of Henle
questions.explanation: ADH increases the permeability of collecting ducts so more water is reabsorbed.

questions.stem: Excess amino acids are deaminated in the liver to form
questions.explanation: The amino group is removed and converted to urea via the ornithine cycle.

questions.stem: The liver stores excess glucose in the form of
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes conversion of glucose to glycogen in the liver.

questions.stem: On a hot day, the skin helps to cool the body by
options: shivering of skeletal muscles and narrowing of the skin arterioles
reducing the activity of sweat glands
sweating and widening of the surface arterioles
increasing fat deposits under the skin
raising the hairs on the skin
questions.explanation: Vasodilation brings blood to the surface, and evaporation of sweat removes heat.

questions.stem: Which hormone lowers the level of glucose in the blood?
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes uptake of glucose and its storage as glycogen.

questions.stem: A child whose thyroid gland produces too little thyroxine is likely to suffer from
questions.explanation: Thyroxine deficiency in childhood causes cretinism.

questions.stem: The "fight or flight" responses such as increased heart rate and widened pupils are caused by
questions.explanation: Adrenaline prepares the body for emergency.

questions.stem: Seedless fruits can be produced by spraying unpollinated flowers with
questions.explanation: Auxins (and gibberellins) can induce parthenocarpy.

questions.stem: Which plant hormone hastens the ripening of fruits?
questions.explanation: Ethylene (ethene) gas promotes fruit ripening.

questions.stem: The part of the brain that controls balance and muscular co-ordination is the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum co-ordinates movement and posture.

questions.stem: Nerves that carry impulses from receptors to the central nervous system are
questions.explanation: Sensory (afferent) neurones carry impulses to the CNS.

questions.stem: The sudden withdrawal of the hand from a hot object is an example of a
questions.explanation: It is a rapid, automatic response via a reflex arc.

questions.stem: In a simple reflex arc, the correct path of the impulse is
options: receptor, motor neurone, relay neurone, sensory neurone, effector
sensory neurone, receptor, relay neurone, effector, motor neurone
receptor, relay neurone, sensory neurone, motor neurone, effector
receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector
effector, motor neurone, relay neurone, sensory neurone, receptor
questions.explanation: Impulses pass from receptor through sensory, relay and motor neurones to the effector.

questions.stem: Salivating at the sound of a lunch bell after weeks of hearing it before meals is an example of
questions.explanation: A learned association between a stimulus and a response is a conditioned reflex.

questions.stem: The part of the eye that contains light-sensitive cells is the
questions.explanation: Rods and cones are found in the retina.

questions.stem: When a person looks at a distant object, the ciliary muscles
options: relax and the lens becomes thicker
relax and the lens becomes thinner
contract and the lens becomes thicker
contract and the lens becomes thinner
questions.explanation: For distant vision the ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments tighten and the lens flattens.

questions.stem: Colour vision and fine detail in bright light are mainly due to cells concentrated at the
questions.explanation: The fovea contains densely packed cones.

questions.stem: The structure in the ear concerned with balance is the
questions.explanation: The semicircular canals detect head movement.

questions.stem: The function of the Eustachian tube is to
options: transmit sound vibrations from the eardrum directly to the cochlea
equalise air pressure on both sides of the eardrum
questions.explanation: It connects the middle ear to the pharynx to balance pressure.

questions.stem: In the human male, sperms are produced in the
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis takes place in the seminiferous tubules.

questions.stem: The stages in the complete metamorphosis of a butterfly are
questions.explanation: Complete metamorphosis includes larval and pupal stages.

questions.stem: The cockroach undergoes incomplete metamorphosis because its life history
options: has a larva and a pupa
has nymphs and no pupal stage
questions.explanation: Incomplete metamorphosis: egg, nymph (several moults), adult.

questions.stem: Which vertebrate group lays eggs with a shell on land and has internal fertilisation but no placenta?
questions.explanation: Reptiles lay shelled (cleidoic) eggs on land after internal fertilisation.

questions.stem: The male part of a flower is the
questions.explanation: The stamen (anther and filament) produces pollen.

questions.stem: In an epigynous flower such as that of the guava, the ovary is
options: borne on a long stalk outside the corolla
absent, so the flower is functionally male
superior, lying above the other floral parts
inferior, lying below the other floral parts
questions.explanation: Epigynous flowers have an inferior ovary with other parts arising above it.

questions.stem: A flower of Hibiscus that has both stamens and carpels and can be divided into two equal halves along several planes is
questions.explanation: Hibiscus flowers are hermaphrodite and radially symmetrical.

questions.stem: The transfer of pollen grains from an anther to a stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species is
questions.explanation: Pollen moves between different plants in cross-pollination.

questions.stem: Which feature is typical of wind-pollinated flowers such as maize?
options: Large feathery stigmas hanging outside the flower
Sticky, spiny pollen grains that cling to the bodies of insects
questions.explanation: Feathery exposed stigmas trap airborne pollen.

questions.stem: In some flowers the stamens mature before the stigma is receptive. This condition, which favours cross-pollination, is called
questions.explanation: Protandry: anthers ripen before the stigma.

questions.topic: Development of the zygote in flowering plants
questions.stem: After fertilisation, the ovule develops into the
questions.explanation: The ovule becomes the seed and the ovary the fruit.

questions.topic: Development of the zygote in flowering plants
questions.stem: In flowering plants the endosperm nucleus is formed when a male nucleus fuses with the
questions.explanation: Triple fusion gives a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

questions.stem: The tomato is described as a berry because it
options: has a hard stony endocarp surrounding a single seed
has a fleshy pericarp with many seeds
questions.explanation: Berries have a succulent pericarp containing many seeds.

questions.stem: The cashew "apple" is regarded as a false fruit because it
questions.explanation: False fruits develop partly from parts other than the ovary.

questions.stem: Pineapple is an example of a
questions.explanation: Pineapple develops from the ovaries of a whole inflorescence.

questions.stem: Fruits of Tridax with a crown of hairs (pappus) are dispersed by
questions.explanation: The parachute of hairs aids wind dispersal.

questions.stem: The fibrous mesocarp of the coconut is an adaptation for dispersal by
questions.explanation: The light fibrous husk allows the fruit to float.

questions.stem: The raw materials for photosynthesis are
questions.explanation: 6CO2 + 6H2O produce glucose and oxygen in light.

questions.stem: The oxygen given off during photosynthesis comes from the
questions.explanation: Photolysis of water releases oxygen in the light stage.

questions.stem: In the dark stage of photosynthesis, carbon dioxide is fixed into carbohydrates using
options: ATP and reduced NADP from the light stage
oxygen released from water during the light stage
questions.explanation: The Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH2 from the light reactions.

questions.stem: Yellowing of leaves (chlorosis) due to a lack of a component of chlorophyll is caused by deficiency of
questions.explanation: Magnesium is part of the chlorophyll molecule.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a micronutrient (trace element) for plants?
questions.explanation: Boron is needed in very small quantities.

questions.stem: The class of food that is mainly needed for growth and repair of body tissues is
questions.explanation: Proteins provide amino acids for building tissues.

questions.stem: Night blindness results from a deficiency of
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed to make visual purple in rod cells.

questions.stem: Kwashiorkor in children is caused by a diet lacking adequate
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor results from protein deficiency.

questions.stem: A pregnant woman is advised to eat more iron-rich foods mainly because iron is needed for
options: haemoglobin formation in her blood and the foetus
strengthening the bones and teeth of the developing foetus
questions.explanation: Iron is a component of haemoglobin, and blood volume increases in pregnancy.

questions.stem: A blue-black colour appears when iodine solution is added to a food sample containing
questions.explanation: Iodine gives a blue-black colour with starch.

questions.stem: A food sample turned violet when dilute sodium hydroxide and a few drops of dilute copper(II) sulphate were added. The sample contains
questions.explanation: The biuret test gives a violet colour with protein.

questions.stem: A brick-red precipitate formed when Benedict's solution was heated with a food sample. The sample contains
questions.explanation: Benedict's test is positive for reducing sugars.

questions.stem: Bile helps in the digestion of fats by
questions.explanation: Bile salts emulsify fats, increasing surface area for lipase.

questions.stem: The dodder plant (Cuscuta), which obtains food from the host through haustoria, is a
questions.explanation: Cuscuta lacks chlorophyll and feeds on its host.

questions.stem: The finger-like projections that increase the surface area of the small intestine are
questions.explanation: Villi increase surface area for absorption.

questions.stem: A herbivore has the dental formula i0/3 c0/1 pm3/3 m3/3. How many teeth does it have in the upper jaw?
The gap between the incisors and premolars in a goat is called the
questions.explanation: Herbivores have a diastema for manipulating food with the tongue.

questions.stem: Amoeba takes in food by
questions.explanation: Pseudopodia surround the food particle to form a food vacuole.

questions.stem: The place where an organism normally lives is its
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home of an organism.

questions.stem: All the Tilapia fish living in a particular pond make up a
questions.explanation: A population is all the individuals of one species in an area.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an abiotic component of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Abiotic components are the non-living factors such as pH.

questions.stem: An edaphic factor is one that is related to the
questions.explanation: Edaphic factors concern soil properties.

questions.stem: Relative humidity of the air is measured with a
questions.explanation: A wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer measures humidity.

questions.stem: The transparency (turbidity) of pond water can be measured using a
options: light meter used in air only
questions.explanation: The depth at which a secchi disc disappears indicates turbidity.

questions.stem: In the chain maize -> grasshopper -> toad -> snake -> hawk, the organism at the fourth trophic level is the
questions.explanation: Maize is level 1, grasshopper 2, toad 3 and snake 4.

questions.stem: Only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next. If producers fix 50 000 kJ, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
questions.explanation: 50 000 x 0.1 = 5000 kJ (primary); x 0.1 = 500 kJ (secondary).

questions.stem: Which type of ecological pyramid can never be inverted?
options: Pyramid of biomass in open water
Pyramid of numbers in a parasite chain
questions.explanation: Energy is always lost between trophic levels, so each level has less than the one below.

questions.stem: The relationship between nitrogen-fixing bacteria and the roots of leguminous plants is
questions.explanation: Both partners benefit: bacteria get food, the plant gets fixed nitrogen.

questions.stem: The cattle egret feeding on insects disturbed by grazing cattle without harming them is an example of
questions.explanation: The egret benefits while cattle are neither helped nor harmed.

questions.stem: The tadpole of a toad is adapted for life in water by having
questions.explanation: Gills allow aquatic respiration and the tail aids swimming.

questions.stem: Acid rain is formed mainly when water in the atmosphere reacts with
questions.explanation: SO2 and NOx dissolve to form sulphuric and nitric acids.

questions.stem: Excessive run-off of fertiliser into a lake often leads to death of fish because
options: fertilisers directly poison the gills of all fish in the lake
algal bloom and its decay use up dissolved oxygen
questions.explanation: Eutrophication: decomposing algae deplete oxygen.

questions.stem: The first organisms to colonise a bare rock surface during primary succession are usually
questions.explanation: Lichens are pioneer organisms that begin soil formation on bare rock.

questions.stem: Secondary succession is observed when vegetation grows again on
options: a new island formed from coral
questions.explanation: Secondary succession occurs where soil already exists after disturbance.

questions.stem: Which of the following will cause an increase in the size of a population?
questions.explanation: Immigration adds individuals to a population.

questions.stem: A village had 2400 people at the start of a year. During the year there were 96 births, 36 deaths, 20 immigrants and 8 emigrants. The population at the end of the year was
Salting fish preserves it mainly because salt
options: raises the temperature of the fish
adds vitamins and minerals that slow down the decay of fish
draws water out of microorganisms by osmosis
questions.explanation: High salt concentration dehydrates bacteria and fungi.

questions.stem: Termites in a colony which are wingless, blind and responsible for building and feeding are the
questions.explanation: Workers carry out building, feeding and grooming.

questions.stem: The release of a tiny parasitic wasp that lays its eggs in cassava mealybugs, reducing their numbers on cassava farms, is an example of
questions.explanation: Using a natural enemy is biological control.

questions.stem: Houseflies and cockroaches are called mechanical vectors because they
options: carry germs on their bodies without the germs developing inside them
are the hosts in which the germs must reproduce sexually before transmission
inject germs directly into the bloodstream through bites
questions.explanation: Mechanical vectors simply transport pathogens on their legs, mouthparts and bodies.

questions.stem: The vector of malaria in Nigeria is the female
questions.explanation: Plasmodium is transmitted by female Anopheles.

questions.stem: Yeast is useful in bread making because it
options: produces lactic acid in the dough
produces carbon dioxide that makes the dough rise
kills harmful bacteria in the flour and the water used
questions.explanation: Fermentation releases CO2 which leavens the dough.

questions.stem: The BCG vaccine given to babies soon after birth protects them against
questions.explanation: BCG is the vaccine against tuberculosis.

questions.stem: Which practice best prevents the breeding of mosquitoes around homes?
options: Clearing stagnant water and blocked gutters
questions.explanation: Mosquito larvae develop in stagnant water.

questions.topic: Microorganisms: Man and His Health (Nigeria extension)
questions.stem: Tuberculosis is caused by a
questions.explanation: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

questions.topic: Microorganisms: Man and His Health (Nigeria extension)
questions.stem: Ringworm of the scalp is caused by a
questions.explanation: Ringworm (tinea) is a fungal infection, not a worm.

questions.stem: The setting aside of land such as Yankari as a protected area for wild animals is mainly to
questions.explanation: Game reserves and national parks conserve wildlife.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a renewable natural resource?
questions.explanation: Forests can be replaced by replanting.

questions.stem: Height in humans is an example of
questions.explanation: Height shows a range of values between extremes.

questions.stem: The ability to roll the tongue is an example of
questions.explanation: People either can or cannot roll the tongue.

questions.stem: Knowledge of blood group variation is applied mainly in
questions.explanation: Matching ABO groups avoids agglutination.

questions.stem: A person with blood group O can safely donate blood to people of all ABO groups because O red cells
options: carry neither antigen A nor antigen B
are smaller than other red cells
carry both antigens A and B
contain antibodies a and b only, which destroy the recipient's cells
questions.explanation: Without A or B antigens, O cells are not agglutinated by recipient antibodies.

questions.stem: The physical expression of a gene, such as tall or dwarf, is called the
questions.explanation: Phenotype is the observable characteristic.

questions.stem: An organism with two identical alleles for a trait, e.g. TT, is described as
questions.explanation: Homozygous means having identical alleles.

questions.stem: A cross between a pure-breeding red-flowered plant (RR) and a white-flowered plant (rr) gives F1 plants that are all red. The F2 phenotypic ratio expected is
questions.explanation: Rr x Rr gives 1RR : 2Rr : 1rr, i.e. 3 red : 1 white.

questions.stem: In a test cross, a black guinea pig is crossed with a white (bb) guinea pig and produces 14 black and 13 white offspring. The black parent must be
options: impossible to tell from these results
questions.explanation: A 1:1 ratio in a test cross shows the black parent carries one recessive allele.

questions.stem: Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes. The number in each sperm cell is
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number.

questions.stem: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes takes place during
questions.explanation: Chiasmata form and exchange segments in prophase I.

questions.stem: Two parents both heterozygous for albinism (Aa) have a child. The probability that the child is albino is
questions.explanation: Aa x Aa gives aa in 1 of 4 combinations.

questions.stem: A couple already has three daughters. The probability that their next child will be a boy is
questions.explanation: Each birth is independent; the chance of a boy is 1/2.

questions.topic: Linkage, sex determination and sex-linked characters
questions.stem: Every normal human egg cell carries
options: an X and a Y chromosome
either an X or a Y chromosome
questions.explanation: Females are XX, so every ovum receives an X chromosome.

forming the bones of the skeleton
